descriptionChirho: Qal verb meaning to ornament or deck oneself with jewelry and finery. Used of Israel as an unfaithful bride adorning herself (Hos 2:13, Ezek 16:11-13, 23:40), of Zion adorning itself with its people as ornaments (Isa 61:10), of Jeremiah's taunt to adorn in vain (Jer 4:30, 31:4), and of God challenging Job to adorn himself with majesty (Job 40:10). All occurrences share the same semantic domain of personal adornment. Consistently translated across languages: Arabic tazayyana (to adorn), Spanish adornarse, Korean kkumida (to decorate), Hindi sajana (to adorn), French se parer. The auto-clusters merely split on inflectional forms (imperative, imperfect, consecutive imperfect) rather than genuine sense distinctions.
